status: Historical speed comparison; superseded by the quality-first default
changes: Candidate graph uses VAEDecode instead of VAEDecodeTiled; verified with FP16 VAE.
Launcher selects FP16 VAE and disables pinned host memory; dynamic VRAM and PyTorch attention remain enabled.
Candidate graph saves only the native image; expensive upscaling is run only for selected PNGs in a separate graph.
Both API files contain executable nodes only at top level and import directly into the frontend.
Visual candidate workflow includes a valid increment-after-generation seed control; API seed remains fixed for reproducibility.
Visual workflows include explicit stage instructions and preserve the reference conditioning graph.
verification_method: Two seeds, 20261026 and 20261027, using fresh then warm runs. Both comparison services used the existing comfyui Conda environment, reserve-vram 0.8, disabled pinned memory and unchanged generation parameters. OS filesystem cache was not cleared. GPU temperature and power were recorded without software temperature/power stopping. No overclock, power-limit, fan-policy or dependency changes.
limits: The original full pipeline and optimized native-only pipeline have different output scopes; the entire latency reduction is not an algorithmic speedup.
The first-run comparison is affected by OS file-cache and model initialization differences; warm-run node timings are more useful.
Tiled versus non-tiled VAE decoding changes some pixels despite identical sampling latents. Visual comparison found the tested composition and identity preserved, not pixel-identical output.
Existing foot/hand anatomy and stylized background risks remain; this optimization does not claim to repair them.
FP16 VAE validity was checked on this installed Illustrious checkpoint, not every other model.
This IPAdapter high-resolution workflow remains much slower than the previously measured simple 1024-square SDXL benchmark; those runtimes are not interchangeable.
verification_service_shutdown: The owned port-8188 verification process was deliberately terminated after both browser jobs succeeded; supervised exit code 15 is cleanup, not a generation failure.
